---
Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity bump, adding EU region, and contract extension options. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, private VPC considerations, and next steps for benchmarks and contract amendment. Transcript quality medium; a few ASR artifacts.
Topics: renewal options, reserved capacity, multi-region onboarding (EU), SLA and security (SOC2/KMS), benchmarking plan, procurement timeline
Action items (high level): see metadata action_items above
---
[00:00] Daniel: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'll kick off real quick. this is the renewal and expansion sync for ember nano, we wanted to align on capacity growth, adding EU region, and what a 12‑month extension would look like.
[00:12] Rajesh: thanks daniel, appreciate it. we have a couple priorities: predictable throughput for our customer facing endpoint, and data residency for EU. also, procurement wants clarity on price delta if we add reserved capacity and a new region.
[00:26] Maya: hi, maya from redwood — i'll be your technical lead on the perf side. quick clarifier: when you say predictable throughput, is this a steady QPS increase or a bursty pattern? helps us pick between dedicated pool sizing vs autoscaling bursts.
[00:39] Lina: mostly steady but with periodic spikes during nightly batch scoring; 3x traffic around product releases. 95th pct latency needs to stay under 220ms for the end user flows.
[00:50] Tom: platform note — we want the EU region in eu‑west and ideally private VPC peering to our VPC; also KMS integration is mandatory for keys at rest.
[01:02] Daniel: got it; so two asks — capacity bump with predictable baseline + burst, and EU private connectivity with KMS. quick outline of options: 1) increase reserved capacity by X GPUs for 12 months; 2) keep current reserved set but enable burst credits and autoscale; 3) move some routes to a cheaper quantized variant for non‑interactive workloads.
[01:25] Rajesh: price sensitivity — what does option 1 look like vs option 2? and what's the risk to latency if we do option 3 with the quantized models?
[01:36] Maya: good q. option 1 gives you predictable cost and headroom — latency stays within current profiles. option 2 saves on committed spend but contention can cause occasional tail spikes; we have fallback routing to lower‑cost regions or model variants but there's a small risk during simultaneous bursts. option 3 (quantization) depends on the model family — for reranking and batch jobs it's very cost effective, for chat generation you'll see quality delta that might show up in our evals. we can run a quant‑A/B if you want. note: our SLO rollbacks and automatic fallback policy are configurable.
[02:10] Sofia: procurement — timeline wise we need final pricing and contract language by Jan 9th to sign before Jan 18th. can you do that?
[02:19] Daniel: yes, we'll aim to send an amendment by Jan 4th so you have time to review.
[02:24] Connor: i'll also add an invoice and seat/route-level cost breakdown to make procurement easier.
[02:32] Lina: regarding EU, can you confirm data residency — logs, transcripts, and KV cache — all stay in EU?
[02:41] Maya: yes, on private deployment or dedicated pools in eu‑west we keep data in region. small caveat: we do collect aggregated telemetry for platform health; that can be filtered or redacted and tokenized per contract. also just noting ASR sometimes writes K V cash in the notes, sorry — that's our ASR bug.
[02:58] Rajesh: (laughs) we read that earlier. on security we need SOC2 type II attestation, SAML/SSO for RBAC, KMS integration, and audit log forwarding to our SIEM. is that all standard?
[03:12] Daniel: yep that's all available — SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML, RBAC and HSM/KMS integrations. we'll attach the security pack.
[03:20] Tom: networking — we prefer VPC peering but also want to understand egress costs if we do cross‑region failover to US. any rough numbers?
[03:31] Maya: egress depends on region pairing and traffic; our proposal will include an estimated egress table. for cross‑region failover we're typically seeing 2–4% incremental cost on token units but depends heavily on your throughput and cache hit rates.
[03:46] Rajesh: on caching — can you remind us of prefix vs KV caching? we saw something about K V cache earlier…
[03:54] Maya: sure — prefix caching stores repeated prompts/responses to hit the token output; KV cache (key‑value cache) holds attention state for ongoing sessions to avoid recomputing — huge latency saver for long chat sessions.
[04:09] Lina: for the nightly batch scoring — can we route that to a quantized model in a different capacity pool? that's where we can accept slightly lower quality.
[04:18] Maya: absolutely — that's a common pattern: route batch scoring to quantized/cheaper backends and keep the interactive routes on full‑quality models. we can also schedule batch jobs during off‑peak windows to lower cost.
[04:29] Daniel: okay, let's talk numbers briefly — current commit is X GPUs (customer obfuscated in transcript), you asked for +40% baseline and the eu region ask. our finance team will model: 12‑month reserved with region add‑on vs 6‑month with bursts. we'll send both price points.
[04:47] Sofia: any penalties for early termination or downsizing? procurement needs flexibility clauses.
[04:53] Connor: we can include a partial pro‑rata clause for the first 60 days of the term and a structured downsize window at the 6‑month mark with a 30‑day notice. i'll draft language.
[05:05] Rajesh: benchmarks — Lina will share the prompt set. we want a throughput run that simulates 300 qps sustained with 1k concurrent sessions. can you support that in your lab?
[05:16] Maya: yes — we'll provision an isolated benchmark window. propose Jan 11th at 08:00 PT for a 2‑hour slot; we'll run steady‑state and spike windows and capture 50/95/99 latencies.
[05:27] Lina: Jan 11th works for the infra team. i'll send the prompt set and test harness by Jan 6th.
[05:34] Tom: small ops question — will dedicated pools have automatic kernel selection and are we able to pin models? we need predictable inference kernels for performance.
[05:44] Maya: yes, dedicated pools allow you to pin model versions and kernel flags; runtime will pick optimized kernels but you can lock to a config for evaluation. we also expose batch size and kv cache configs.
[05:56] Daniel: wanted to surface a competitor note — Rajesh mentioned they are evaluating Anthropic and VertexAI for certain workloads; we heard that earlier in RFP. if helpful, we'll include a short comparatives sheet in the packet.
[06:11] Rajesh: yes, we saw both — vendor decisions will be hybrid by workload. pricing and SLA tilts the balance.
[06:19] Sofia: procurement question — if we add EU region mid‑term, will billing be consolidated or separate invoice?
[06:27] Connor: consolidated billing is standard; we'll call out region surcharges as line items.
[06:33] Lina: one more technical callout — for long running sessions, do you recommend larger KV cache or sticky routing? we've had regens when KV cache warms up slowly.
[06:45] Maya: sticky routing with session affinity helps; larger KV cache reduces cold starts but memory usage increases. we can show tradeoffs in the perf matrix.
[06:53] Daniel: ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[06:56] [Recap]
[07:00] Daniel: action 1, we'll send the 12‑month and 6‑month options with EU add on by Jan 4th. action 2, maya will run benchmarking plan and share runbook by Jan 7th. action 3, lina to send prompt set and SLO targets by Jan 6th. action 4, connor to draft flexible downsize language by Jan 4th.
[07:20] Rajesh: sounds good. quick question — is there any chance to get an interim trial of EU region before commit? maybe a 30‑day eval?
[07:30] Daniel: we do limited pilot capacity for enterprise prospects; we can provision a short pilot for EU private pool subject to procurement and NDA timing. we'll include that option in the amendment.
[07:42] Sofia: procurement will push for the 30‑day pilot so legal can exercise the integration.
[07:48] Daniel: perfect. any final questions?
[07:50] Lina: no, thanks.
[07:52] Tom: no.
[07:54] Rajesh: thanks everyone.
[07:56] Daniel: thanks all — we'll follow up on the action items. have a good afternoon.
